- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism; especially after recent supply auctions.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >70), model tends to overshoot and continue upward — cap forecast growth to 0.5–1.0% per day post-spike.
- If official event net supply is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model should not ignore downward pressure — adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per event horizon.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon: if forecast is >75 and true outcome drops below 70, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until price stabilizes.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and event supply is negative, model should not assume continuation — forecast should be conservative, with 0.5–1.0% downward bias.
- If multiple consecutive auctions (e.g., 3+ in 10d) with negative supply net, model should reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per auction to reflect supply shock.
- Forecast should not assume sentiment will persist — if sentiment drops below 0.33, reduce forecast slope or cap at 70–72 range unless policy change occurs.
- In 30d horizon, if true outcome deviates >3% from 30d mean, adjust forecast to mean-revert toward 70–74 range unless strong bullish sentiment or policy event overrides.
